--[[
The one fused JSON decoder, monomorphized per builder.

The structural scan and the tape walk are identical across the pull, serde,
and eager decoders; only the builder constructor varies. `Variant` carries
that choice as a const binder: each exported entry closes it with a literal,
so ahead-of-time compilation emits one specialized native body per variant,
with the untaken variants' constructs pruned before lowering classifies the
entry.

The scan is the vector/bitmask algebra `bench/simd-json/src/simd_json/indexer.nupp`
is written in. One vector of bytes at a time, every byte the scan has to act
on -- a quote, a backslash, a control byte or one of the six structural
characters -- is found by comparisons whose masks are or'd together and read
out as one word of lane bits. The bits are drained in position order, lowest
first, and each event byte is fed to a byte-at-a-time state machine that
keeps string state and backslash parity. Bytes that are not events are never
touched by the drain, which is where the vectors earn their place.

UTF-8 is validated in the same vectors rather than in the drain, by the
lookup4 validator that `bench/utf8simd/src/utf8simd.nupp` implements with the
general algebra and simdjson uses. Every byte's verdict depends on itself and
the three before it, so the two nibbles of the previous byte and the high
nibble of this one index three tables of error-class bit sets, and the pair is
malformed exactly when the three sets share a class. The third and fourth
bytes of a scalar are the one case a pair cannot see, so those are checked
against the bytes two and three back and folded in with an xor. A validated
block ending in ASCII owes no continuation, so the next block only needs the
lookup if it contains a non-ASCII byte. Otherwise the lookup also checks the
boundary, without first reducing the current block's high-byte mask.

After an ASCII-ending block, the scan combines non-ASCII and structural
masks. An empty result skips both the high-byte reduction and the drain.
A nonempty result distinguishes Unicode and removes its bits before draining:
Unicode is validated as a vector, never walked byte by byte on that path.
A non-ASCII byte outside a string is refused by the tape walk below as the
syntax error it is, and one inside a string is only bytes.

Whatever the vectors do not cover -- the partial vector past the last whole
one, and every byte on a target without vectors -- the same loop finishes one
at a time, so the drain is written once and events are processed in byte
order across both. There the drain does validate UTF-8, from an owed
continuation count and a first-continuation constraint seeded at the hand-off
by looking back over the at most three bytes of a scalar the last whole
vector could not finish. Either way the first scan error in the input is
reported at the one-based position of the byte that raised it.

Every operation here is the general algebra's. The loads read a `Span<uint8>`
over the entry's own rooted bytes, which `valuebuilder.bytes` returns: a
value-building entry's parameters cross the Lua stack, where a pointer and a
count are not values, so the span is made from the parameter rather than handed
in. A whole vector is loaded unchecked under the same `cursor + species.lanes <=
length` guard the loop already runs on.

A vector therefore cannot cross an iteration of the scan loop, because the
species only exists inside the branch that found one. The previous vector, which
the lookup needs for the three bytes before each byte it judges, is read again
instead of carried; before the first vector that load is out of range and
returns zeros, which is what a scan that has seen nothing needs.
]]

Standard base64.

```nupp

const text = base64.encode("Nupp")
```

--- Encodes bytes as standard base64, padded.
---
--- ```nupp
--- assert(nupp.codec.base64.encode("Nupp") == "TnVwcA==")
--- ```
--- @param value the bytes to encode
--- @return the encoded text
--- @export

end

--- Decodes canonical standard base64 with required padding.
---
--- Text that is not canonical padded base64 is an ordinary answer, as it is for
--- `nupp.codec.hex.decode`: nil and the reason.
---
--- ```nupp
--- assert(nupp.codec.base64.decode("TnVwcA==") == "Nupp")
--- local bytes, reason = nupp.codec.base64.decode("TnVwcA")
--- assert(bytes == nil and reason ~= nil)
--- ```
--- @param text the text to decode
--- @return the decoded bytes, or nil when the text is not base64
--- @return why the text is not base64, when it is not
--- @export
function base64.decode(text: string): (string?, string?)
    if #text % 4 ~= 0 then
        return nil, "base64 input length is not a multiple of four"
    end
    local decoded = decodeAot(text, INVALID)
    if decoded == INVALID then
        return nil, "base64 input is not canonical padded base64"
    end

    return decoded as string, nil
end
